package.title: Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea? New Phase 3 Results #shorts
package.description:
Two Phase 3 trials (NEJM, Oct 20, 2026): in adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and a BMI of 27 or higher, with or without type 2 diabetes, retatrutide cut breathing pauses and shallow breaths per hour more than placebo over 80 weeks. Common side effects: nausea, diarrhea.

Retatrutide isn't approved anywhere yet. On July 23, 2026, Lilly said it plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027. Filing isn't approval. Tirzepatide (Zepbound) has been FDA-approved since Dec 20, 2024 for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity; common side effects include nausea, diarrhea and constipation. Separate trials, not head-to-head.

On CPAP? Don't stop or change it on your own; ask your sleep clinician.

Sources:
https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2611477
https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-medication-obstructive-sleep-apnea

factcheck.summary: The script is accurate and safe, and the facts I checked hold up. NEJM published "Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea" (TRIUMPH-1-OSA, n=243, and TRIUMPH-2-OSA, n=448) on Oct 20, 2026. Both trials enrolled adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and a BMI of 27 or higher, without or with type 2 diabetes. Both ran 80 weeks against placebo, and in both retatrutide lowered the AHI more than placebo. Adverse events were mainly gastrointestinal and mild to moderate. Lilly's July 23, 2026 release says it plans to submit a BLA to the FDA in Q1 2027. As of October 2026 nothing has been filed and nothing approved. The FDA approved tirzepatide (Zepbound) for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity on Dec 20, 2024, and the FDA lists nausea, diarrhea and constipation among its common side effects. Framing is good: "not head-to-head", "filing isn't approval", a CPAP safety line, and the disclaimer plus the prescriber line. I found only minor polish items: give the trial sizes, date the "not approved" status, add one line against gray-market products (retatrutide is widely sold online as a research chemical), and make the CPAP card less absolute. The NEJM page returned 403 to my direct fetch, but search results confirm the title, the DOI URL, the date and the findings.

issues.claim: One without diabetes, one with type two diabetes... Retatrutide versus placebo, eighty weeks.
issues.problem: No trial sizes are given. The craft rules ask for each group's size, and NEJM reports 243 participants in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and 448 in TRIUMPH-2-OSA.
issues.fix: Narration: "One trial of two hundred forty-three adults without diabetes, one of four hundred forty-eight with type two diabetes. All had moderate-to-severe sleep apnea and a B-M-I of twenty-seven or higher. Retatrutide versus placebo, eighty weeks." stat_label: "Retatrutide vs placebo, 80 weeks: TRIUMPH-1-OSA (n=243, no diabetes) & TRIUMPH-2-OSA (n=448, type 2 diabetes); moderate-to-severe OSA, BMI 27+"

issues.claim: Common side effects: stomach issues like nausea and diarrhea.
issues.problem: This is accurate but leaves out the source's severity qualifier (mostly mild to moderate). The myth card, "Retatrutide only helps weight", is also a mild strawman.
issues.fix: Narration: "Common side effects: stomach issues like nausea and diarrhea, mostly mild to moderate." Myth: "It's only a weight drug". Fact: unchanged.

issues.problem: The status isn't dated, so it will go stale. There is also no line warning viewers about the retatrutide being sold online as a 'research peptide', which this audience is likely to come across.
issues.fix: Narration: "As of October twenty-fourth, twenty twenty-six, retatrutide isn't approved anywhere, so anything sold online as retatrutide isn't an approved medicine. On July twenty-third, twenty twenty-six, Lilly said it plans to file with the F-D-A in the first quarter of twenty twenty-seven. Filing isn't approval." on_screen_text: "Not approved anywhere (as of Oct 24, 2026)".

issues.claim: On-screen text: full approval, population, side effects and 'not head-to-head' on one card
issues.problem: The card has too much text to read on a Short. It needs splitting so every item stays readable.
issues.fix: Split into two cards: "Tirzepatide (Zepbound): FDA-approved Dec 20, 2024, adults with moderate-to-severe OSA + obesity" then "Common: nausea, diarrhea, constipation | Separate trials, not head-to-head".
